key_insight: Medical imaging AI hallucinations are a cross-modality safety problem that require unified taxonomy, careful detection, and lifecycle-based mitigation.
clinical_relevance: Hallucinated findings, laterality errors, and fabricated measurements can directly affect diagnosis, biopsy decisions, staging, and treatment planning.
method: Synthesized peer-reviewed studies, benchmark datasets, and FDA guidance across five imaging modalities.
Compared hallucination taxonomies and failure modes across the imaging pipeline.
Mapped mitigation strategies to FDA Total Product Lifecycle and Predetermined Change Control Plan oversight.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that general-purpose foundation models outperformed medical-specialized models on hallucination-specific benchmarks, and that many AI-generated flags still needed expert correction.
watch_item: Medical fine-tuning may reduce generality and increase confabulation, so deployment needs human oversight and regulatory lifecycle monitoring rather than one-time validation.
paper_title: Hallucination in Medical Imaging AI: A Cross-Modality Analytical Framework for Taxonomy, Detection, and Mitigation under Regulatory Constraints
